segments.text: Big idea. While earthly powers and a counterfeit priesthood strike at the continual mediation
to Mede of our high priest, Daniel 814 announces that after 2300 prophetic years,
the heavenly sanctuary will be vindicated and cleansed, neat stock, through Christ's pre-advent
judgment on the anti-typical day of atonement. From The Last Sitting, Sitting 7. In Sitting 7,
Daniel saw four predatory beasts rise from a storm-tossed sea, tracing the succession
of world empires from Babylon to Rome, followed by the 1260-year supremacy of the Little Horn,
538 to 1798 AD, and the convening of the celestial court before the ancient of days.
Now in Chapter 8, in the third year of Belshazzar, Daniel 8 slash 1, circa 551 B.C.,
the prophetic camera narrows from the geopolitical turmoil of nations to focus upon God's sanctuary
itself, unveiling the cosmic conflict between an earthly, counterfeit priesthood and Christ's high
priestly ministry in the heavenly tabernacle. Introduction. The vision at the River Uli in
Susa. Daniel 8 slash 1 through 3. Susa. Third year of Belshazzar. Year reconstructed. In the third
year of King Belshazzar's reign, Daniel was at Shushan in the palace, which is in the province
of Elam by the River Uli. Daniel 8 slash 2. Shushan is the Hebrew name of Susa, which later
became a Persian royal city, Esther 1 slash 2, Nehemiah 1 slash 1. There, Daniel witnessed a
striking prophetic drama involving a two-horned ram, a swift rough goat, and a little horn that
magnified itself even to the prince of the host. A title this sitting explains below.
Notice immediately the profound sanctuary atmosphere established by the imagery.
Whereas Chapter 7 utilize unclean wild predators, lion, bear, leopard, monster,
Chapter 8 employs clean, domestic sacrificial animals, a ram and a he goat.
In the Levitical sacrificial system, Leviticus 16.3 names a young bullock for a sin offering
and a ram for a burnt offering, and Leviticus 16.5 names two kids of the goats for a sin offering
and one ram for a burnt offering for the supreme service of the day of atonement.
That was the one day each year when the high priest entered the most holy place,
the inner room of the sanctuary, to make atonement for the people and for the sanctuary itself,
Leviticus 16. This intentional choice of symbols alerts the reader that the ultimate theological
destination of Daniel 8 is not merely geopolitical conquest but the day of atonement cleansing of
the sanctuary. Main point one, the named ram and goat, Medo-Persia and Greece, Daniel 8 3 through
8, 20 through 22. In Daniel 8, the angel Gabriel whom God sent to make Daniel understand
the vision, Daniel 8 16, names the empires that the animals stand for. The names are written in the
text itself so the reading does not rest on guesswork. The ram which thou saw having two horns
are the kings of Media and Persia, and the rough goat is the king of Grisha,
and the great horn that is between his eyes is the first king, Daniel 8 20 through 21.
One, the two-horned ram, Medo-Persia 539 through 331 BC. Daniel saw a ram standing before
the river having two horns. Both horns were high, but one was higher than the other, and the higher
one came up last, Daniel 8 3. As Gabriel confirmed, the ram represents the dual monarchy of Media and
Persia. Gabriel does not say which horn is which. History suggests that the higher horn that arose
last is the Persian dynasty under Cyrus the Great, which rapidly overshadowed its median
partners. The ram pushed westward, northward, and southward, and doing according to its will
so that it became great, Hebrew Higdil, Daniel 8 4, conquering Lydia, Babylon, and Egypt.
Two, the shaggy goat, Greece under Alexander the Great, 331 to 323 BC. Suddenly, a male goat came
from the west across the face of the whole earth without touching the ground,
possessing a notably large horn between its eyes, Daniel 8 5. Coming from the west, Europe, at
such speed that its feet did not touch the earth, the goat portrays the breathtaking conquests of
Alexander the Great, the first king of United Grisha, Daniel 8 21. In 334 to 331 BC, Alexander's
Greco-Macedonian phalanxes crossed the Hellespont, shattered the Persian forces at the Granicus,
Issus, and Gagamela. The goat attacked the ram in fury, broke its two horns,
and trampled it underfoot. Alexander waxed very great, Hebrew Higdil, Daniel 8 8.
The broken horn and the four successor horns, 323 to 301 BC. Scripture records that when he
was strong, the great horn was broken, Daniel 8 8. At the very zenith of his military triumph,
Alexander died in Babylon in June 323 BC. In place of the broken horn arose four notable
successor horns toward the four winds of heaven, Daniel 8 8. Gabriel explains,
four kingdoms shall stand up out of the nation, but not in his power, Daniel 8 22. After more than
two decades of civil war among Alexander's generals, the Diatoki, the empire was partitioned
following the battle of Ipsis, 301 BC, into four distinct Hellenistic realms,
Cassander, Macedon Greece, Lysimachus, Thrace, Asia Minor, Seleucus, Syria, Mesopotamia,
and Ptolemy, Egypt, Palestine. Main point two. The little horn roam in two successive phases,
Daniel 8 9 through 12, 23 through 25. Daniel 8 9 says, and out of one of them came forth a little
horn, which waxed exceeding great toward the south and toward the east and toward the pleasant
land. The KJV's ascending wording is great, very great, and exceeding great. Exceedingly great is
the New King James wording, not the KJV. The escalation is therefore in the text itself,
not an artifact of English style. The Medo-Persian ram became great, Higdiel 8 4. The Grecian goat
became very great, Higdiel with Mioed 8 8. The little horn waxed exceeding great, Daniel 8 9.
On the historicist reading, which this course follows, this little horn is
roamed in both of its successive historical phases, pagan and papal. It is the same power as the
little horn of Daniel 7, seen from another side. Daniel 7 followed its papal phase for 1260 years,
and Daniel 8 adds the pagan phase before it. The horn comes out of one of the four Greek
kingdoms, Daniel 8 9 out of one of them. Rome began in the west, but it grew by taking over
the Greek kingdoms one by one. So this reading says the horn grows out of the Greek world.
The pleasant land is Judea. This reading calls the horn Rome because it grows greater than
Persia and Greece, and because its reach matches the directions in the verse.
South into Egypt, 30 BC, east into Syria, 64 BC, and into Judea, 63 BC. First, that is the empire
that crucified Jesus and burned the temple. Then it is the church power that sets itself against
Christ's ministry in heaven by hiding the truth about it. The next point explains how.
The two phases of Rome in Daniel 8, phase one horizontal expansion, imperial pagan Rome,
Daniel 8 9. Emerging from the western Mediterranean, Rome expanded horizontally toward the south,
absorbing Egypt in 30 BC, toward the east, annexing the Seleucid realm of Syria in 64 BC,
and toward the pleasant land, subjugating Judea under Pompey in 63 BC. It was pagan Roman
authority under Pontius Pilate that delivered Jesus Christ, the prince of the host,
to crucifixion at Calvary. Pagan Roman legions under Titus besieged Jerusalem and burned the
earthly temple to the ground in 70 AD. Phase two vertical expansion, ecclesiastical
slash papal Rome, Daniel 8-10-12. The horn then grew vertically upward toward heaven.
It waxed great even to the host of heaven and it cast down some of the host and of the stars
to the ground and stamped upon them, Daniel 8-10-12. This represents the religious phase of Rome,
persecuting the saints of God, the stars, exalting itself to equal the prince of the host,
removing the continual daily mediation, Tamed, casting down the truth to the ground and
establishing an earthly, sacerdotal counterfeit. We have come to the first checkpoint.
Main point three. The assault on the Tamed, usurping Christ's heavenly priesthood.
Daniel 8-11-12, Hebrews 7-25, 8-1-2, 1 Timothy 2-5. The core spiritual crime of
the little horn is described in Daniel 8-11-12 with surgical precision. Yea, he magnified himself
even to the prince of the host and by him the daily sacrifice was taken away and the place of
his sanctuary was cast down. And in host was given him against the daily sacrifice by reason
of transgression and it cast down the truth to the ground and it practiced and prospered.
Daniel 8-11-12. The English translators supplied the word sacrifice in italics.
It is not in the Hebrew. The word is ha-tamid, the continual. That note sits beside the verse.
It is not inside the KJV warding. The prince of the host is the commander of heaven's army.
Daniel 8-25 calls him the prince of princes and Daniel 9-25 calls the Messiah the prince.
This reading takes all three titles to be Jesus Christ.
What is the Tamed? In the Old Testament earthly sanctuary, the Tamed represented
the continual uninterrupted priestly ministry before God. The morning and evening burnt offering,
Exodus 29.38-42. The perpetual burning of the golden candlestick, Exodus 27.20.
The continual incense ascending before the veil, Exodus 30.8. And the continual showbread upon
the golden table, Leviticus 24.8. It symbolized the unbroken perpetual mediation between God and
his people. In the New Testament anti-type, the true Tamed is the continual high priestly
intercession of Jesus Christ in the heavenly sanctuary. Hebrews declares,
Wherefore he is able also to save them to the uttermost that come unto God by him,
seeing he ever liveth to make intercession for them. Hebrews 7.25.
Christ is the sole minister of the true tabernacle. How did the papal little horn
take away the Tamed? A human power cannot climb into heaven and pull Christ off his throne.
On this reading, the papal system instead hid and replaced the truth about Christ's continual
heavenly work by setting up a counterfeit priesthood on earth. The reading names four ways.
An earthly priesthood that offers a sacrifice at an altar in place of Christ's one priesthood in
heaven. Treating the work of priests at the altar as a continuing offering, though Christ's
sacrifice on Calvary was finished once for all. Hebrews 9.26.10.12. Asking people to confess their
sins to a priest instead of confessing directly to our high priest in heaven. 1 John 1.9. Asking
Mary and the saints who have died to pray for us in place of the one mediator between God and
men, Christ Jesus. 1 Timothy 2.5. By putting human priests, earthly altars, and church
traditions between the believer and the heavenly sanctuary, this reading says the little horn
casts down the place of his sanctuary in people's understanding and casts down the truth to the
ground. In other words, the attack is on what people believe about Christ's work in heaven,
not on heaven itself. We have come to the second checkpoint. Main point four. Refuting
Antiochus the fourth epiphanies. Scale, horizon, and sanctuary. Why the Preterist
reading, the view that places the prophecy in the past, as Sitting Zero explained, say the little
horn of Daniel 8 is Antiochus the fourth epiphanies. He was a king of the Seleucid dynasty, one of the
four Greek kingdoms that followed Alexander, and he ruled from 175 to 164 BC. He defiled the Jewish
temple, set up an altar to Zeus, and sacrificed pigs. In 164 BC, a Jewish rebel leader, Judas
Maccabeus, and his men cleaned the temple and rededicated the altar. The reading taken in this
course disagrees, and it is a minority view among scholars today. The cards below give four tests
that Antiochus fails. He was never greater than Persia and Greece. The vision reaches the time of
the end, not 164 BC. The 2300 days do not fit his few years, and the word for the sanctuary's
cleansing means to be vindicated, which a washed altar is not. Daniel 825 adds one more line. It
says, the horn shall be broken without hand by no human power. Antiochus's death in 164 BC may look
like a match, but it cannot settle the question, because the four tests already show that he is too
early and too small for the whole vision. The breaking in this verse belongs with a power
that lasts to the time of the end. Test one. The progression of greatness, the scale criterion.
The text demands a power far mightier than Medo-Persia and Greece. Medo-Persia became great,
8.4. Greece waxed very great, 8.8. The little horn waxed exceeding great, 8.9.
Antiochus Epiphanes was not the exceeding great horn. His dynasty fought Rome and lost.
The Treaty of Amaea in 188 BC imposed indemnity on his father Antiochus III,
and Antiochus IV himself had been a Roman hostage. When Antiochus invaded Egypt, the Roman ambassador
Popilius Linus confronted him, drew a circle in the dirt around him, and demanded that Antiochus
pledge to abandon Egypt before stepping out of the circle. Antiochus humiliated himself and obeyed.
He was never greater than Cyrus or Alexander. Rome, pagan and then papal, is the power that
grew exceeding great. Pagan Rome ruled the known world, and the papal phase, which sitting seven
followed for 1,260 years, held power over the kings of Europe. Test two. Gabriel's time horizon,
the chronological criterion. Gabriel explicitly locks the vision of Daniel VIII not to the
horizon, and the verses that stand beside it. Understand, O Son of Man, for at the time of the
end shall be the vision. Daniel 8.17. And I have heard the man's voice between the banks of Uli,
which called and said, Gabriel, make this man to understand the vision. Daniel 8.16.
Wherefore shut us thou up the vision, for it shall be for many days. Daniel 8.26.
In this course, the time of the end means the last stretch of history before Christ returns.
Sitting 10 dates its start at 1798. A local crisis in Judea in the 160s BC cannot exhaust a
prophecy that Gabriel locked to that time. Test three, the 2,300 days versus Antiochus'
three years, the span criterion. The temple was defiled under Antiochus' epiphanies for about
three years, 167 to 164 BC. But 2,300 days is more than six years, twice as long. To make the
rhetoric cut the 2,300 and a half to 1,150 days by counting each evening sacrifice and
each morning sacrifice as a separate day. That having is added to the verse. The Hebrew phrase
eta bokeh, evening morning, names one whole day, as in Genesis 1.5, the evening and the
morning were the first day. So the verse says 2,300 days. In a symbolic vision, a day stands
for a year. Numbers 1434, Ezekiel 4.6, explained in Sitting Zero. So that is 2,300 years,
a span long enough to run from the Medo-Persian age to the time of the end.
Test four, the word nitstock, the sanctuary criterion. Under Antiochus, the earthly altar
in Jerusalem was defiled. And in 164 BC, it was cleaned and rededicated. That is the washing
of a building. But Daniel 8.14 does not use the ordinary Hebrew word for cleaning a place.
It uses nitstock, which means to be put right, justified, or vindicated. That is a word from
the courtroom. The verse says the sanctuary will be vindicated, not scrubbed. The last section of
the sitting explains the word in full. Main point five, nitstock and 2,300 prophetic years,
the day of atonement in heaven. Daniel 8.13-14, Leviticus 16.30, Hebrews 8.1-2, 9.23-26.
In his vision, Daniel heard one saint speaking and another saint asking,
how long shall be the vision concerning the daily sacrifice and the transgression of desolation
to give both the sanctuary and the host to be trodden underfoot? Daniel 8.13.
The divine answer echoed through heaven. And he said unto me, unto 2,300 days,
then shall the sanctuary be cleansed. Daniel 8.14, KJV. The Hebrew verb under cleansed is
nitstock. That lexical note sits beside the verse. It is not inside the KJV wording.
Linguistic precision, nitstock versus Tahar. The English King James version translates the
Hebrew verb, nitstock, as cleansed. However, the Hebrew verb for physical washing or ceremonial
cleansing is Tahar. Daniel was inspired to use nitstock, a passive form of the root tzedok,
meaning to be justified, to be vindicated, to be declared righteous, or to be restored
to its rightful state. Other forms of the same root appear in courtroom settings. Deuteronomy
25.1 speaks of judges who justify the righteous, and Job 4.17 asks whether a man can be more just
than God. Nitstock, a passive form of that root, is the verb of Daniel 8.14. Daniel 8.14 does
not speak of scrubbing stone floors with water. It announces the vindication, as in a court of
law, of the heavenly sanctuary, God's character, and his covenant people against the blasphemous
claims of the little horn. The Day of Atonement shows how the sanctuary comes into this. On that
day the priest cleansed two things. He cleansed the people, Leviticus 16.30, for on that day shall
the priest make an atonement for you, to cleanse you that ye may be clean from all your sins
before the Lord. And he also made atonement for the holy place, the tabernacle and the altar,
Leviticus 16.16.33. Daniel 8.14 names the second of these, the sanctuary itself.
This reading takes it as the heavenly counterpart of the earthly Day of Atonement.
It is the same court scene that sitting seven saw in Daniel 7.9-10,
where the judgment was set and the books were opened.
The calculation, 457 B.C. to 1844 A.D. Under the biblical year day principle,
Numbers 1434, Ezekiel 4.6, explained in Sitting Zero, the 2,300 evening's mornings represent
2,300 literal solar years. But Daniel 8.14 gives a length with no starting date, and the chapter
ends with Daniel unable to understand the vision, Daniel 8.27. In Daniel 9, Gabriel comes back and
says, understand the matter and consider the vision, Daniel 9.23. The only vision still
unexplained is this one. He then gives a shorter period, the 70 weeks, and says it is determined
for Daniel's people, Daniel 9.24. The Hebrew word means cut off. He also gives its starting point,
the going forth of the commandment to restore and to build Jerusalem, Daniel 9.25.
If the 70 weeks are cut off from the 2,300, both begin at the same place. This reading takes
that starting point to be the decree of Persian king Artaxerxes I in 457 B.C.,
Ezra 7.11-26. The next sitting shows the whole chain step by step.
Now add the years. Start at autumn 457 B.C. and count 2,300 years forward. The calendar has no
year zero between 1 B.C. and A.D. 1, so add one more year. The minus sign below stands for B.C.
1944 American Experience. Mistaken event, verified timetable.
The Millerite Awakening. In the 1830s and early 1840s, a Baptist farmer preacher named
William Miller alongside Joshua V. Himes and Samuel S. Snow studied Daniel 8.14. Relying
on historicist principles, they correctly calculated that the 2,300 years would terminate in 1844.
Snow named October 22, 1844 as that year's Day of Atonement, the tenth day of the seventh month on
the Karaite calendar. Karaite reckoning is the calendar he used for that date.
The mistaken event, the great disappointment. The Millerites assumed that the sanctuary was the
earth and that its cleansing meant the purification of the earth by fire at the second coming of
Jesus. When Christ did not appear in the autumn of 1844, believers endured disappointment.
The biblical resolution, prayerful re-study of the Bible by those believers, remembered above
all in Hiram Edson's account, set down years afterwards, led them to see that Scripture never
calls the earth the sanctuary. The sanctuary of Daniel 8.14 is the heavenly sanctuary,
Hebrews 8.1-2, 9.23-24. In 1844, on this reading, Jesus began the last part of his work
in heaven. The most holy place is the inner room the Day of Atonement entered. That work is the
heavenly judgment Daniel 7.9-14 already showed and the cleansing of the sanctuary before he returns.
The cross remains the one's sacrifice. Christ, in plain words, the little horn attacks the
sanctuary for 2,300 days and then the sanctuary is put right. Daniel 8 answers a question no one
asks out loud in the chapter, how long will the attack on God's sanctuary last? The answer given
is, unto 2,300 days, then shall the sanctuary be cleansed. Daniel 8.14. Notice where the attack
lands. The little horn does not content itself with land or treasure. It grows toward the
pleasant land, takes away the daily sacrifice, and casts down the place of the sanctuary,
Daniel 8.9-11. The regular ministry of the sanctuary is the target. That is why the answer
is measured in sanctuary time and why it ends with the sanctuary put right. Two steps make
this reading work, and this course states both plainly. First, the span is given in days with
no starting point, and Daniel says he did not understand it, Daniel 8.27. Second, in Daniel 9,
Gabriel returns and tells him to consider the vision, Daniel 9.23. Then gives the 70 weeks as
a period cut off and supplies a starting decree, Daniel 9.24-25. If those weeks are cut from the
2,300, both begin together, and this reading takes the starting decree to be the decree of
Arteserxes in 457 BC, Ezra 7. On the year-day scale, the 2,300 days are 2,300 years,
which is why the count reaches 1844. The bottom line is what cleansed means. The Hebrew verb is
and it is the language of a court rather than a bucket, to be vindicated, to be put right.
So the last word of this chapter is not that a building was scrubbed. It is that God's name,
his sanctuary, and his people are cleared of the horns' charges.
Anyone who has ever been accused has a stake in that word.
The Day of Atonement work of 1844 is Christ's final priestly ministry, not a repetition of the
cross. At Calvary, Jesus offered the once-for-all, all-sufficient sacrifice for human sin, Hebrews
926. The earthly Day of Atonement shows the order. First the sacrifice, then the priest
carries the blood into the sanctuary. Christ made the one sacrifice on Calvary, and now,
as our great High Priest, he appears in the presence of God for us, Hebrews 924,
to vindicate his people and cleanse the sanctuary. Look by faith into the Most Holy Place,
the inner room that the Day of Atonement entered, where Christ ever lives to intercede
for you. We have come to the third checkpoint. Practical Application, Entering the Heavenly
Sanctuary by Faith. Daniel 8 transforms our understanding of Christ's present ministry
and the hour of history in which we live. 1. Rely exclusively on Christ's continual
intercession. The papacy offers human substitutes for the tamede. Do not look to human priests
to make you right with God. Jesus Christ is your living High Priest. Approach his throne
of grace directly with confidence, Hebrews 4, 14-16. 2. Live with sober reverence while the
judgment is underway. On this reading, since 1844, Christ has been carrying out the heavenly
counterpart of the Day of Atonement, and the whole universe is watching how God handles it.
In ancient Israel, the Day of Atonement was a time of prayer, fasting, and deep searching
of heart. You shall afflict your souls and do no work at all, Leviticus 1629.
Live with reverent faithfulness, knowing that your life is open before the heavenly court,
covered by the blood of Christ. 3. Do not shrink Daniel 8 to one ancient king.
Do not reduce Daniel 8 to Antiochus IV. God's prophetic map spans from ancient empires,
through the cross, to our own generation, and the glorious second advent.
4. Rest in the final vindication of God's people. The word knitstalk says the sanctuary
will be put right. When error seems to prosper and compromise abounds,
remember that the sanctuary is being cleansed, God's justice is being revealed,
and His everlasting kingdom will soon prevail. The Principle to Remember
Text. Does Daniel 814 promise that after 2300 prophetic days, the sanctuary will be knitstalk,
vindicated, cleansed? History. Did the 2300 solar years span from the 457 BC decree to the
anti-typical Day of Atonement in 1844 AD? Interpretation. Does the progression of
greatness, became great, waxed very great, waxed exceeding great,
prove the horn is Rome rather than Antiochus? Christ.
Is Jesus Christ your living high priest in the heavenly sanctuary,
whose once for all sacrifice at Calvary covers you in the judgment? Christology.
The Great High Priest in the Heavenly Sanctuary. Daniel 8 unveils the assault of the little horn
power upon the prince of the host, casting down the place of his sanctuary, taking away the daily
intercession, and casting truth to the ground. Daniel 8, 11-12. The prince of the host is Jesus
Christ. In response to this counterfeit earthly priesthood, heaven proclaims the divine remedy.
Unto 2,300 days, then shall the sanctuary be cleansed. Daniel 8, 14.
The Hebrew nitsdak means put right. This points not to an earthly building in Jerusalem,
but to the true tabernacle, which the Lord pitched, and not man. Hebrews 8, 1-2.
The Day of Atonement Cleansing of the Sanctuary in 1844 is Christ's final priestly work,
not a repetition of the cross. On Calvary, Jesus offered the once for all,
all sufficient sacrifice for human sin. Hebrews 9, 26. But an atonement requires both sacrifice
and priestly ministry. In the Heavenly Sanctuary, our Great High Priest applies his shed blood,
blotting out the recorded sins of his people and cleansing the sanctuary before the universe
prior to his glorious return. Enter boldly by faith into the Most Holy Place, where Jesus
ministers on your behalf. Do not allow human traditions or priests in place of Christ's
intercession to obscure Christ's direct and living mediation. Confess your sins honestly to
him today. He is faithful and just to forgive and cleanse you from all unrighteousness.
Live with reverent joy, knowing that our High Priest is finishing his work of reconciliation
and will soon step out of the sanctuary to receive his waiting people.
